question: Is gemma-4-26B-A4B's disagreement with llama.cpp a runner fault, or the model amplifying ordinary numeric differences?
method: All rows: 16 prompts x 16 greedy tokens, compared by token id. 'self (runner)' perturbs only the KV cache precision inside one binary; 'self (llama.cpp)' changes only cold vs warm prefix cache. Both are smaller perturbations than switching engines.
conclusion: Not a runner fault. On the certified 26B, runner disagrees with ITSELF on 11 of 16 prompts from a KV-cache precision change alone - MORE than the 9 it disagrees with llama.cpp on. A perturbation strictly inside one binary moves the output further than switching engines does, so the cross-engine gap has no room left to attribute to an implementation fault. Direct checks agree: layer 0's attn_norm matches the reference exactly, and the pre-softmax router logits match to ~0.1-0.5%. The amplifier is discrete top-8-of-128 routing over Q4_0 weights: at layer 2 the 6th and 7th selected experts sat 0.0002 apart in weight, so a rounding difference flips an expert and changes an eighth of the FFN output.
caveat: The README's 'token-identical to llama.cpp' claim for gemma-4-26B-A4B-it does NOT reproduce at b10076: reference_compare gives 4/5 on the certified file. No archived artifact backs the original claim, and the dense gemma-4 claim in model.c cites b9964, a different revision. Given the sensitivity floor above, exact-text identity is not an achievable gate for this model on any engine pair.
